transcript:
Header
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Elysian Procurement), Priya Nair (Elysian CISO), Aisha Khan (Elysian Legal), Tom Reynolds (Elysian VP Eng)

Summary: Procurement/legal review focusing on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets for dedicated vs hosted inference, pricing approval path, and onboarding timeline. Action items and next steps captured at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll give a quick agenda - MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs and target latency, pricing commit numbers, and onboarding timeline. we have ~45 minutes.
[00:12] Marcus: Sounds good. quick ask - we need to get the legal checklist closed by mid January for our board sign-off.
[00:16] Sofia: understood. Priya and Aisha are on the call, so we'll work through the security and legal points now. Daniel will cover the SLA/technical bits.
[00:24] Daniel: hi team. small note, i'll also send the benchmark spreadsheet after - it's p50/p95 numbers across our hosted and dedicated profiles.
[00:30] Tom: great. we mostly care about 99th latency for chat and throughput for batch embeddings.
[00:35] Priya: quick security top-line: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention, KMS integration, and data residency (US-only). are those supported out of the box?
[00:44] Daniel: yes. Redwood hosted supports SOC 2, SSO via SAML, audit logs streaming to customer's SIEM, and KMS integration for Private deployments. small caveat: for hosted we encrypt at rest with our managed KMS; for Private VPC you can bring your own KMS/HSM.
[00:59] Priya: okay, for Elysian we need BYOK and HSM option - legal will want explicit language in DPA around key control.
[01:06] Sofia: noted - we'll add BYOK/HSM call-outs in the DPA redline.
[01:11] Aisha: on the MSA, section 8.2 liability cap - typical SaaS cap is 12 months of fees; Elysian will need 18 months and an exception for data breaches. we can start there and see if Redwood can make a concession.
[01:24] Sofia: thanks. typically Redwood's standard is 12 months but we can take 18 months to finance. i'll flag to legal.
[01:30] Marcus: also procurement needs payment terms 60 days net and PO process. any issues?
[01:35] Sofia: we can do net 60 for enterprise deals with procurement approval. we'll note that in the contract.
[01:40] Tom: on the SLA side - what are the uptime guarantees for Dedicated vs Hosted and do you offer credits?
[01:46] Daniel: Hosted API has a 99.9% SLA for availability; Dedicated has 99.95% with optional reserved capacity SLA. credits are prorated as service credits in the MSA; we can share exact SLA doc.
[01:56] Priya: uptime is fine, but we need latency SLOs for model serving - e.g. conversational workloads need p95 < 300ms, otherwise user experience degrades. can Redwood commit?
[02:06] Daniel: we usually commit p95 targets based on model + instance profile. for our curated models on Dedicated with a 4xA100-equivalent pool we can hit p95 ~200-300ms for shorter context chat. for hosted we estimate p95 between 250-400ms depending on load. we'll put numbers in the SLA appendix.
[02:22] Marcus: and if latency increases due to burst traffic, what are fallback policies?
[02:26] Daniel: Redwood has smart routing - we can route to a cheaper/compatible model variant or fallback to cached responses. for mission-critical paths you can pin to Dedicated or enable automatic burst capacity.
[02:36] Aisha: DPA question - retention and deletion. we need guaranteed deletion of customer prompts and embeddings within 30 days of request and audit logs showing deletion. is that possible?
[02:46] Daniel: yes for Private/VPC, BYOK, you control persistence; for hosted we have options to disable retention and we can show deletion workflows. we'll include deletion attestation in DPA. small transcript note: sometimes the transcriber writes KV cache as K-V cash.
[02:58] Tom: haha okay noted.
[03:00] Priya: encryption in transit and at rest covers us, but we also need to know where data is stored - we require US-only data residency.
[03:07] Daniel: we support region pinning; hosted US-only region available. Private deployment of course stays in your VPC and can be on-prem.
[03:14] Marcus: pricing - we are seeking a committed monthly spend tier to get discounts. procurement wants a 12 month committed contract with volume tiers and an option to expand. what do you propose?
[03:24] Sofia: typical enterprise commit: committed monthly spend with tiers for token consumption and discounted rates for embeddings. i can share a starter pricing sheet. if you commit to a baseline we can offer 12-18% discount on token rates and lower embedding unit cost.
[03:35] Marcus: what about overage? we need predictable billing, preferably auto-billing to a PO with alerts before hitting thresholds.
[03:41] Sofia: you can set spend alerts in the console, and overage is billed at the committed tier's overage rate. we can also cap spend and route to a lower-cost model once cap reached.
[03:49] Aisha: legal redlines for the DPA: breach notification window needs to be 48 hours, not 72. can Redwood accommodate 48?
[03:57] Sofia: i'll take that back. standard is 72 hours, but for enterprise customers we've accepted 48 in some cases. we'll propose 48 in the DPA redline.
[04:05] Priya: audit rights - we need SOC 2 report and right to audit within reason. also, we require subprocessor disclosures.
[04:13] Daniel: Redwood maintains a subprocessors list and we can provide quarterly updates; SOC 2 Type II report can be shared under NDA.
[04:20] Tom: quick technical: for embeddings throughput and dedicated batch jobs - do you support hardware pinning for heavy embedding pipelines?
[04:27] Daniel: yes, Dedicated allows GPU pool pinning; you can also reserve node types for embeddings with higher batch size and throughput. we'll include recommended configs.
[04:35] Marcus: procurement path - once legal signs off on MSA/DPA we still need pricing approval from finance. timeframe likely 1-2 weeks for approvals if docs are final. we need a firm onboarding start date by Jan 23. doable?
[04:46] Sofia: yes, if we get final docs by Jan 10, we can start onboarding the week of Jan 23. onboarding includes a pilot: 4-week pilot, integration support, and a post-pilot review.
[04:58] Aisha: on onboarding, legal wants data flow diagrams and a runbook for incident response. can you share those?
[05:05] Daniel: absolutely, we'll share architecture diagram, data flow, and IR runbook (redacted where needed).
[05:11] Priya: SLA credits language - we need concrete examples of credits and escalation path (pager, on-call).
[05:18] Sofia: we'll include contact list and escalation matrix in the SLA appendix; on-call pager can be added as part of enterprise support add-on.
[05:25] Marcus: procurement also asked about subcontractor insurance limits and indemnity. Aisha will send specifics after.
[05:31] Aisha: yes - i'll send insurance minimums and any required vendor attestations by EOD tomorrow.
[05:36] Daniel: one more technical note - if you move to Private on-prem, there is an offline installer and an ops playbook; otherwise VPC deployment is fastest.
[05:45] Tom: latency expectations for Private on-prem are best, right?
[05:49] Daniel: correct, on-prem or VPC w/ local GPUs will minimize cross-region hops so p95 is lowest. but costs shift to customer infra.
[05:56] Marcus: ok that's fine.
[06:00] Sofia: to recap - action items: Sofia will send MSA with proposed 48hr breach and 18-month cap concession, Daniel sends benchmark and runbooks, Priya shares SOC2/DPA comments, Aisha sends insurance and DPA redlines. we aim for legal finalization by Jan 10 and onboarding week of Jan 23.
[06:18] Priya: that's correct. one last question - do you have a standard data processing addendum template we can start from?
[06:24] Sofia: yes i'll attach the DPA template with the MSA redline.
[06:28] Marcus: any blockers on finance for committed spend? we need a rough number to start budget approval.
[06:33] Sofia: i'll include a pricing workbook with 3 scenarios - pilot (light), production minimal commit, and production high. Marcus, you can pick the scenario and we can tailor discounts.
[06:42] Aisha: legal would prefer to see the final DPA first before pricing is locked, but we'll proceed in parallel.
[06:49] Sofia: great. we'll follow the parallel path.
[06:52] Tom: can you also include an option for a trial dedicated capacity week-of-Jan 23 as part of onboarding?
[06:58] Daniel: yes we can provision a short dedicated pool for pilot, subject to capacity. we'll mark that request in the spreadsheet.
[07:05] Marcus: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:08] Sofia: thanks all. we'll send materials this week. next touchpoint: legal-only review week of Jan 10 - calendar invite to follow.
[07:16] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels generic, occasional transcription mis-hearings (e.g., K-V cache as K-V cash), and punctuation dropped in places.

Recap & Final Next Steps:
- Sofia to send MSA + DPA redlines (call out BYOK/HSM, 48hr breach, 18mo liability cap proposal) by 2027-01-04.
- Daniel to share benchmark spreadsheet (p50/p95 numbers, cost per 1k tokens) and onboarding runbook by 2027-01-06.
- Priya to provide SOC 2 Type II and encryption/KMS architecture notes by 2027-01-08.
- Aisha to send consolidated DPA redlines and insurance requirements by 2027-01-08.
- Legal-only sync to be scheduled week of 2027-01-10.
- Target onboarding/pilot start: week of 2027-01-23 (4-week pilot).

Action items repeated for clarity in action_items field above.
